literal: If one obtains those who, looking into the mind, understand what has occurred, it is sufficient to stand looking at their face.
translation: If one can find companions who can look into the mind and perceive what has occurred within, it is enough to merely stand looking at their face.
modern: மனதைப் பார்த்து உள்ளே நிகழ்ந்ததை உணர்ந்து கொள்ளும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களைப் பெற்றால், அவர்கள் முகத்தைப் பார்த்துக்கொண்டு சும்மா நின்றாலே போதுமானது.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extraordinary value of having companions or advisors who can read minds. If a person is fortunate enough to find those who can look into the mind ('அகம் நோக்கி') and instantly understand what is felt or what has happened ('உற்றது உணர்வார்'), then spoken words become unnecessary. Simply standing before them and looking at their face ('முகம் நோக்கி நிற்க') is completely sufficient ('அமையும்') to communicate. The poet beautifully contrasts the deep inner perception of the wise with the effortless outer presence required of the seeker.
